_comment: Operator-maintained configuration for the finances_* tools. Data, not code:
correct a rate, a due date or a cadence here and redeploy the config; no
Python change needed.
Seeded 2026-07-30 from the finances repo's PLAN.md; revised 2026-07-31 after
the first live verification session (see that repo's DECISIONS.md).
Five sections:
hurdle_rate  the APR above which a debt is worth accelerating rather than
paying on schedule. Everything at or below it is cheap money
and gets 'ride'.
debts        which accounts count as debt, and what each one costs. An
account is treated as debt only if it is BOTH listed here AND
carrying a negative balance, so the House and the investment
accounts can never be swept in. Negative-balance accounts that
are NOT listed are still reported, under `unlisted`, rather
than silently dropped.
sync         per-account expected feed cadence. 'daily' feeds are stale
after a few days; 'monthly' feeds (statement exports) are
healthy for weeks; 'manual' accounts never sync at all and are
excluded from the verdict. Judging a monthly feed by a daily
rule is what made the overall verdict permanently 'dead'.
pulse        non-secret matching policy for pulse-specific aggregates.
recurring    expected fixed obligations, checked against what posted.
_floor_excluded_categories_comment: Categories that are ALLOCATION or OBLIGATION, not consumption, and so
are excluded from the floor comparator and reported separately.
PLAN.md's floor accounting puts these in bucket 3.
Savings/Investments — counting a 529 or brokerage contribution as
spend would penalize exactly the behaviour the plan wants more of.
Taxes — a prior-year balance or an estimated payment is an obligation
being settled, not a month's discretionary choice. The $19,116.32 IRS
payment of 2026-08-03 would otherwise read as a ~$19k overspend in the
One list, consumed by finances_monthly_summary AND finances_room via
the shared bucketing, so the two can never disagree about what counts.

_comment: rate              APR percent. null means UNKNOWN — the tool refuses to
classify it rather than guessing, because calling a
carried card balance 'ride' would be actively wrong.
is_variable       true if the rate moves on its own (prime-pinned etc.).
These are the ones whose classification can change
without anyone touching this file, so a flip is
reported loudly.
scheduled_payment the normal monthly payment, dollars. null if none.

Spectra HELOC.note: Prime-pinned; interest-only minimum. The only expensive debt.

Mortgage (NewRez).note: Irreplaceable rate — never prepay or refinance.

Tesla Loan (Santander).note: Manual off-budget account; balance updated by hand.

_cards_comment: Purchase APRs from the 2026-08-01 statements. Every one is far above the
5.0 hurdle, so ANY balance that survives the grace period classifies
'accelerate' — which is the intended signal: revolving on a card is the
most expensive money in the household, well past even the HELOC's 6.75%.
A card sitting at $0 has no negative balance and so never appears at all.
is_variable is true because US card APRs are prime-pinned and reprice on
their own. It does not change any classification here (all are far above
the hurdle); it marks them as rates that can move without anyone editing

_comment: Feed health is judged on `last_sync` — the bank feed's last successful
fetch, which Actual records per account. That is the real signal.
Transaction age is only a proxy, and a misleading one: a dormant card
with a perfectly healthy feed looks identical to a broken one. Both are
reported, but only `last_sync` decides the verdict.
Accounts with no `last_sync` are not bank-linked. If declared 'manual'
below they are excluded outright; otherwise the tool falls back to
activity age and says so, rather than silently passing them.
default_tolerance_pct is the band, as a percent of the expected amount,
within which a posted charge counts as MATCHED. Flat dollar bands were the
original design and were too wide to catch what this tool exists to catch
(FirstEnergy posted 45% over and read MATCHED against a +/-$300 band).
tolerance_pct     per-item override. Widen ONLY for genuinely seasonal
bills. A widened band never hides the delta: any charge
more than default_tolerance_pct off expectation is
reported under `notable_variances` even when MATCHED.
min_tolerance     dollar floor, so small bills don't churn on rounding.
expected_day      day of month it normally posts, or null if it floats.
window_slip_days  {before, after} — for drafts that straddle a month
boundary. Re-anchors the search window on expected_day
instead of the calendar month, so a payment that clears
on the 1st is credited to the month it is FOR. Windows
for consecutive months cannot overlap, so a payment is
never counted into two months. Omit it for bills that
post comfortably inside their month.
match_any         payee substrings, case-insensitive, matched against
payee OR notes. Several are deliberately ugly because
that is what SimpleFin delivers.
accounts          restrict to these account names. On such an account the
servicing payment is the POSITIVE leg, so magnitude is
compared rather than sign.
ends              final month expected, 'YYYY-MM'. Past it the item is
ENDED, not MISSING, so a finished loan stops alarming.

items.name: Electric — FirstEnergy
items.note: Genuinely seasonal (summer AC / winter heat), so the band is wide. The delta is still surfaced under notable_variances whenever it exceeds the default band — a wide band must never mean a silent price rise.

items.name: USAA P&C insurance
items.note: ONE combined monthly draft covering two policies: auto $198.89/mo ($1,193.32 per 6-month term, both vehicles) plus jewelry personal-property $16.58/mo ($199/yr). 198.89 + 16.58 = 215.47 exactly. The jewelry policy WAS the entire draft until 2026-05-01, which is why the old baseline was $16.58; the auto policy joined it when Tesla Insurance was dropped. Observed: 16.58/mo Oct 2025-Apr 2026, then 215.51 (5/1), 215.47 (6/2), 215.47 (7/1). The auto side REPRICES ~Nov 2026 — the amount will change then, and that is expected rather than an anomaly. Tolerance is deliberately the standard 10%: unlike FirstEnergy this draft is contractually flat between repricings, so any variance is signal.

items.name: USAA life insurance
items.note: Drafts on the 28th and posts anywhere from the 28th to the 3rd of the following month, so its billing window is anchored on the 28th rather than the calendar month. Under calendar months the observed series (9/30, 10/30, 12/2, 12/30, 1/30, 3/3, 3/31, 4/30, 6/1, 6/30) read as three MISSING months (Nov, Feb, May) with three other months holding two payments — the charge attributed to the month it CLEARED rather than the one it is for. Consecutive anchored windows cannot overlap, so a slipped payment is claimable by exactly one month. Two payee forms: the clean 'USAA Life Insurance' and the raw descriptor 'USAA.COM PAY INT LIFE' + masked account, which lands in the NOTES field; matching spans payee and notes, substring and case-insensitive.

items.name: RV insurance — Progressive
items.note: Progressive Select policy 968303393, verified against the renewal declarations page dated 2026-02-09. CONFIRMED 12-MONTH TERM, 2026-04-04 to 2027-04-04, so 338.68 is locked until April 2027 — the earlier 'provisional, might be a 6-month term' caveat is retired. Covers ONE vehicle: the 2021 Entegra Coach Aspire, VIN 4VZAU1D9XMC089960. Nothing else rides on it. Amount reconciles, per the renewal cover letter's printed payment schedule: 12-month premium and fees are 4,015.85 (4,004.00 premium + 11.85 MAIF recoupment), plus a flat 5.00 installment fee on each of 12 payments = 60.00, for a total term cost of 4,075.85. The payments are NOT uniform — 350.39 on 2026-04-04, then 338.68 for ten months, then 338.66 on 2027-03-04 — so do not expect 338.68 x 12. The expectation is set to 338.68 because that is 10 of the 12; the 338.66 sits 2 cents inside the band, and the odd first payment of each term is absorbed the same way. The CASH number is the right expectation here; the declared premium would read as a permanent CHANGED. Added 2026-08-07 after the RV-as-consumption decision found it absent from both this config and PLAN.md's fixed table, landing in the register categorized Fixed while nothing watched it for repricing. It hid because it charges the Apple Card — worst-covered account, history starts 2026-05-03, monthly statement export — leaving only the 5/4 and 6/4 observations. Standard 10% band for the USAA P&C reason: contractually flat between terms, so any variance is signal. DO NOT move this draft to checking to tidy the floor: one of its five discounts is Automatic Card Payments, and it must stay on a card to keep it. Next reprice is the renewal declarations page ~Feb 2027, effective 2027-04-04.

_comment: PLAN.md's fear metric, verbatim: cleared USAA Checking - all revolving
card balances - the next mortgage payment. Checking ONLY. No HYSA (it is
earmarked for the Kubota loan), no brokerage, no anything else —
'operations run on checking, full stop'.
CLEARED, not register: the buffer answers 'could we clear the decks
today', and money the bank has not confirmed cannot clear anything.
Only NEGATIVE card balances count. A card carrying a credit is not cash
you owe, and adding it as cash would overstate the buffer.
Synchrony is deliberately absent: those are fixed 0% instalments on a
schedule, not revolving balances that could be called tomorrow.
Deposits into checking whose payee matches NONE of these are breach
candidates: money arriving from HYSA, brokerage or the HELOC to cover
operational spending. The May 2026 $30.7k brokerage sale is the
canonical case. Detection only — the tool never clears or judges one.
Substring match, case-insensitive, against payee and notes. Keep this
list tight: a too-broad entry silently suppresses a real breach.
Annual/irregular costs amortized at 1/12 into the gap. PLAN.md DEFINES
the Bonus Dependence Gap with amortization ('monthly baseline spend,
including 1/12 of annual lumpy expenses'), so the raw monthly gap
understates it in every month one of these does not happen to land.
annual_amount null means NOT YET QUANTIFIED: the entry is listed so it
is not forgotten, and excluded from the arithmetic so it cannot invent
a number. Fill it from statements, don't estimate it here.

items.name: Jayme's baseball membership
items.note: Paid by Zelle to Dustin Pease in instalments to stay under the daily Zelle limit; $2,500 observed (PLAN.md).

items.name: Dental (Natural Dentist Associates)
items.note: $9.1k observed across May-Jul 2026 (ortho/implants?) — that is a treatment episode, not a known annual run-rate. Quantify from the treatment plan before amortizing; guessing would move the household's headline metric on a fiction.

_comment: finances_reconcile compares Actual's register against the bank's OWN
reported balance (via the sidecar's /simplefin-balances). That is what
catches the Jan-Apr 2026 class of fault: a register that drifted from
reality while every transaction was 'cleared'.
settlement_window_days — drift is normal float when it is smaller than
the account's gross activity over this many days. A big deposit or a
card payoff moves both sides at different moments.
market_valued_accounts — investment accounts whose bank balance is live
market value while Actual's register only moves when a transaction
posts. Drift there is valuation, not error, and would otherwise report
five false 'structural' faults on every run.
pending_inclusive_accounts — feeds whose reported balance includes
PENDING items while their transaction feed is cleared-only, so some
drift is expected by construction. USAA Checking is the documented
case. This explains expected drift; it does not license unlimited
drift, so such an account is still escalated past
pending_alert_threshold.
Employer-tied asset concentration — the number a fiduciary planner
opens with. Facts only: this section reports the figure and its
components. Whether it is acceptable is a judgment for humans and
professionals, not for a tool.
CRITICAL, and the reason employer_tied_accounts is an explicit list
rather than a name-match on 'Microsoft': the Microsoft 401(k) is
invested in a TARGET-DATE FUND. It is NOT employer stock and must
never be counted as concentration — it is the single largest account,
so counting it would roughly quintuple the reported figure and make
the metric worse than useless.
msft_shares_in_brokerage is a DOLLAR value maintained by hand: the
Fidelity Brokerage holds vested RSUs still in MSFT, and feeds carry
the account balance but not its positions. Refresh it at monthly
reviews, like the House valuation. null means UNKNOWN — the tool then
reports concentration as 'unknown' and still shows the ESPP figure,
rather than reporting a falsely-low percentage.
